why: A session that never gives the slot back. `attach()` replaces `live` on the next session, so a Campaign<->Versus switch still behaves -- what breaks is the LAST session: after the final teardown the trampolines still dispatch into a disposed input controller, renderer and audio director. 1 of 405 in the scoped run, 'a tap after the LAST session reaches nobody, rather than a disposed one'. Its sibling 'a tap reaches the LIVE session once' deliberately survives this and falls to dropping `live = state` from `attach()` instead -- measured both ways, because the two mechanisms back each other up and reading either as the control for both would claim coverage that is not there. Re-measured at 2 of 421 in loop.test.ts: the second case is "quitting a versus match leaves a campaign-shaped Main Menu behind", because the menu's page shape is restored from `detach()`, which a session that never gives the slot back never reaches.
